summary: Exact irreducible surface gluing criterion; pinch same-centre fibre and uniform coercivity barrier.
detailedSummary: All continuous obstacles on the irreducible self-crossing surface admit a greatest C/D minorant exactly when normal-envelope conductor values agree. Pinch surface CE holds over every field; pinch threefold has a precise two-point same-centre fibre in characteristic not two. Normal coercivity blocks the proposed plateau method and uniformly bounds raw negative envelopes, but same-centre and general normal dimension-at-least-three CE remain open.
text:
Use ENTIRE qualified G331 and n1--n3. These deductions do not assert that every nonsingleton normalization fibre obstructs envelopes.

For the self-crossing SURFACE of n3 over any field of characteristic different from2, or its excellent DVR version with2 invertible, EVERY finite continuous signed obstacle f has an exact criterion. Its normalization S is a semilocal DOMAIN with two regular normal SURFACE centres. The boundary is their disjoint union and the C/D classes are their products by G331; disconnected boundary pieces do not require algebraic idempotents in S. Let H_+,H_- be the continuous geometric envelopes of the pulled-back obstacles, existing by n1's normal-surface theorem. The conductor quotient is the marked DVR k[z]_(z), or V, so the sole nontrivial boundary fibre is o_+,o_- over o. Set a=min(H_+(o_+),H_-(o_-)). Then the COMPLETE raw target C/D supremum equals H_i(w) when w(u)<infinity on centre i, and equals a at o. A greatest geometric C or D minorant exists iff H_+(o_+)=H_-(o_-); when it exists it is continuous and belongs to C.

For the positive lower bound, do not assume fibrewise minima are psh. If a=0, G331's normal zero dichotomy gives both H_i=0 and zero descends. If a<0 and H_i(o_i)<0, set B_i=(a/H_i(o_i))H_i, whose ratio is>=1 and B_i<=H_i. If H_i(o_i)=0, then H_i=0 and use constant B_i=a. These are C functions with B_i(o_i)=a. For n>=1 and integer N>=max(1,n||H_i-B_i||), define G_(i,n)=max(B_i,H_i-w(u)/n), interpreting the second term as bottom when u is killed. Exactly G_(i,n)=max(B_i,H_i-w((u)+a_i^N)/n), because H_i-N/n<=B_i. The ideal term has ACTUAL negative effective relatively ample primary positivity on EVERY contracted curve; G331 addition, scaling and maxima prove G_(i,n) belongs to C. The tuple has common conductor value a and is constant on EVERY fibre. Full-fibre POSITIVE descent gives a target C minorant. These minorants reach H_i at finite-u points and retain a at o; no increasing-limit closure is used. Every target D competitor pulls back below H_i and has common value<=both H_i(o_i), proving the upper bound.

If the conductor values agree, H_i itself descends to the continuous greatest envelope. If H_i(o_i)>a for one centre, finite-u points are dense by divisorial density and continuity of H_i gives a net to o_i with limiting raw value H_i(o_i)>p(o). Thus p is not USC and no greatest C/D minorant exists. This proof also applies to excellent reduced local surfaces with regular normal SURFACE centres, FULL infinite-conductor boundary consisting of one lift per centre over a single target point, and a nonzero conductor element u whose killed locus at each centre is just that point. These full-fibre/local-cone hypotheses are retained; no arbitrary conductor-minimum theorem is claimed.

Now compute the pinch family independently. For ANY field k let R=k[t^2,ty,y,s]_(t^2,ty,y,s) and S=k[t,y,s]_(t,y,s). R is a DOMAIN with presentation k[u,x,y,s]_(u,x,y,s)/(x^2-u y^2), u=t^2,x=ty. The quadratic is irreducible because u is not a square in k(u,y,s), including characteristic2; the subring embedding and rank-two normal form also prove the presentation. Integral t satisfies t^2=u and equals x/y in the fraction field. Thus S is finite, normal and birational, hence the normalization. Its UNIQUE marked centre is the origin because t^2,y,s vanish only there above the target maximal ideal.

With A=k[u,y,s], S_0=A direct-sum tA and R_0=A direct-sum tyA. Membership of a+tb in R_0 requires b divisible by y; multiplication by t additionally requires a divisible by y. Hence the conductor is exactly yS, whose target ideal is (y,x); the finite-module annihilator calculation localizes. Its quotient map is k[u,s]_(u,s)->k[t,s]_(t,s), u->t^2. The target maximal primary gauge (u,x,y,s) extends to (t^2,y,s). Every source and quotient support remains.

For char(k)!=2 there is an EXACT two-point FULL boundary fibre within this ONE marked normal centre. Let alpha have support (y,t-s), beta support (y,t+s), and give s value1 in their k[s] quotients. Both normalize the extended gauge by min(2,infinity,1)=1. Both kill the conductor and restrict to the target support (x,y,u-s^2), with u-value2 and s-value1. Their restrictions agree on EVERY R-element because x,y vanish and t^2=s^2 in both quotients; local units have value0. They differ because alpha(t-s)=infinity while beta(t-s)=1. There are exactly two lifts: modulo that target support, t^2=s^2 has exactly the primes t=+s and t=-s; their quotient fraction fields are k(s), on which the given base valuation has its unique identical extension. Both marked centres are still (t,y,s). This is a concrete same-centre residual, not an instance of n2.

Without s, the pinch SURFACE k[t^2,ty,y]_(t^2,ty,y) has conductor yS and quotient map k[u]_(u)->k[t]_(t). Each quotient centred boundary is a singleton. G331 finite-conductor uniqueness therefore makes normalization restriction bijective on the FULL boundary. At the conductor point the source has w(t)=1/2,w(y)=infinity for gauge (t^2,y), giving target u-value1. Positive order/isometric transport and n1's arbitrary-field normal-SURFACE CE prove continuous geometric envelopes for ALL continuous signed obstacles on this irreducible nonnormal pinch surface over EVERY field. The conductor is nonprimary. In characteristic different from2 the conductor quotient is separable degree two and is not falsely called radicial.

In characteristic2, the threefold quotient k[u,s]->k[t,s] is finite radicial. Every polynomial in t,s has its square in k[u,s] without k being perfect, so its value is forced to be half the value of that square; the same holds for quotient fields and every support. Thus the FULL normalization boundary map is bijective. CE is equivalent to normal-source CE, without a new arbitrary-characteristic threefold CE conclusion. The characteristic-not-two two-point fibre is not asserted in characteristic2.

There is a quantitative same-centre obstruction to the proposed METHOD, distinct from an envelope counterexample. On ANY excellent NORMAL local centre A with primary gauge a, choose normalized centred divisorial nu. G331 supplies K_nu>=1, independent of w, with nu(I)<=K_nu w(I) for every unit-or-primary ideal and EVERY normalized w on that SAME centre. Indeed nu(f)<=C ord_m(f), m^r contained in a and w(m)>=1/r give K_nu=C r after normalization; units are zero. Therefore every geometric C/D function satisfies g(w)<=g(nu)/K_nu throughout that centre. If F(nu)=-D with D>K_nu, EVERY minorant and its raw supremum are <=-D/K_nu<-1 EVERYWHERE. Competitors cannot approach -1 even on a dense subset there.

More concretely, if proposed separators j_n satisfy nu(j_n)>=c n, the element order bound gives w(j_n)/n>=c/K_nu for EVERY w. Thus max(-b,-1-w(j_n)/n)<=max(-b,-1-c/K_nu)<-1 when b>1. Powers of a nonunit cannot be shallow on one region and uniformly deep at a fixed divisorial point in the same marked centre. A local element is a unit at all centred valuations or a nonunit at all; CRT units cannot separate those lifts. This proves why n2's separate-centre argument cannot simply be reused at the pinch threefold's alpha,beta.

A general NORMAL/higher-dimensional deduction follows without CE. If finite continuous f on an excellent normal local domain is negative anywhere, continuity and divisorial density give centred divisorial nu with f(nu)<0. The uniform bound gives -max(0,-min f)<=p(f)(w)<=f(nu)/K_nu<0 on EVERY support. If f>=0, p(f)=0. Therefore the raw supremum has uniform strict negativity in the nonzero case. The same conclusion holds for an excellent nonnormal germ whose finite normalization has a SINGLE marked normal local centre, by pulling back f and all competitors. This includes the pinch test. It proves boundedness and excludes mixed-zero raw patterns; it does not establish USC, continuity, D attainment or greatest-minorant existence.

Finally, when source continuous envelopes are known and a particular pulled-back obstacle's source envelope is constant on EVERY normalization fibre, G331 positive descent gives a continuous target envelope: every target competitor pulls back below it and its compatible descent is a competitor. This is sufficient in the pinch threefold with smooth algebraically closed characteristic-zero source using n1's exact BFJ CE. Necessity is not asserted there. Same-centre nonsingleton-fibre classification and general excellent NORMAL dimension>=3 CE or qualifying failure remain OPEN. Products, energy, full finite operators and literal radial identification remain separate. Artifacts n4.md and n4.tex. Rerun: python assemble.py; python verify_delivery.py. Structural and coercivity claims are proofs relative to G331; finite arithmetic does not settle the residual envelope problem.
